# ci-compute-github

**Own the pipeline's GitHub surface and run targets on Actions.**

A forge-ci `compute` engine.

## Why it exists

The workflows a pipeline runs on are part of the pipeline, so they must
follow it: this engine templates every workflow file from its spec, declares
it beside the Actions secrets and enablement it needs, and the manager
realizes the lot at bootstrap and re-converges it on every apply. A
hand-edited workflow drifts back to what the spec says.

## Tools

| Tool | Does |
|---|---|
| `declare` | Answer one converged file per owned workflow, one Actions secret per declared secret, and enablement for every workflow file. |
| `run` | Dispatch the runner workflow with a unique marker and the target script, correlate by the marker in the run name, and poll to conclusion. |

## By hand

```sh
echo '{"spec":{"repo":"o/r","runner":{"name":"ci-runner","secret":"FORGE_CI_GITHUB_TOKEN"}}}' \
  | ci-compute-github declare
```

## In a pipeline

```yaml
engines:
  - alias: my-compute
    type: compute
    engine: "forge://github.com/alexandremahdhaoui/forge-ci/cmd/ci-compute-github@v0.1.1"
    manager: local
    spec:
      repo: <string>
      dir: <string>
      apiBaseURL: <string>
      tokenEnv: <string>
      ref: <string>
      setup: <list>
      workspace: <object>
      container: <string>
      secrets: <list>
      workflows: <list>
      runner: <object>
```

## Worth knowing

A remote run that concludes red is a run with status failed, never an
error: an error means the machinery broke. The dispatched script is built
through the same target-to-command mapping the local compute uses, every
token single-quoted, with the revision's member shas pinned first - and a
dirty revision is refused outright, because a remote runner can never see
uncommitted changes.

Workflow content is templated from the spec; a workflows entry may instead
carry verbatim `content:`, which wins. Three kinds exist: `command` (build
the workspace, run a command, optionally push what it wrote), `fan-out`
(repository_dispatch to every consumer on a tag) and `release` (tag and
publish, fully generic).

Everything this engine declares goes to its one manager, which must know
the github kinds - route it to ci-manager-github.
